curriculum.lesson_evidence: Strategy is a plan to help a team succeed. In games, using space means moving into open areas, spreading out to make room for passes and closing gaps when defending. Strategies are decided before the game and changed during it based on what is happening. A good strategy is fair, uses everyone and follows the rules.

lesson.child_mission: Strategy is a plan to help a team succeed. In games, using space means moving into open areas, spreading out to make room for passes and closing gaps when defending. Strategies are decided before the game and changed during it based on what is happening. A good strategy is fair, uses everyone and follows the rules.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A team bunches together near the goal. Suggest a strategy that uses space better and say why it works.

FEEDBACK
Spread out so passes can go to open teammates and defenders have more ground to cover. Bunching means one defender can mark everybody. Spreading uses the whole space.

WATCH FOR
Believing the ball should always go to the player closest to the goal. Passing to open space or to a free teammate often works better.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Draw a game space and plan two strategies for attack and two for defence. Play a mini game with family, use each strategy, record what happened in a table and choose the strongest.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.
